newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus oil team in Iraq looks at possible buys.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus oil team in Iraq looks at possible buys.

text.p: An official delegation from Cyprus is in Iraq looking at the potential of resuming oil purchases halted in 1990, Cypriot oil sources said on Monday.
"The delegation left yesterday and will come back tomorrow," said the source, who asked not to be identified.

The Cypriot team wants to be briefed on how much oil Iraq can allocate Cyprus, he added. The team is comprised of a representative from the Cyprus Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Tourism, one representative of the Cyprus refinery and two representatives of local oil importing companies.

The "oil-for-food" agreement, which took effect on December 10, permits Iraq to sell $2 billion dollars worth of oil over six months to buy food, medicine and other necessities to offset the effects of sanctions imposed after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
"Most of Cyprus' oil imports were from Iraq before the sanctions were imposed," said the official, putting Cypriot demands then for Iraqi oil at around 600,000 tonnes per year.
